source.title: Form Trigger execution succeeds but editor remains stuck on "Waiting for you to submit the form"

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body: ### Bug Description I am running a self-hosted n8n instance using Docker on Windows 11 pro. When testing a workflow that starts with a Form Trigger, the form submission succeeds and the workflow executes successfully. However, the n8n editor does not update to reflect the completed execution. The editor remains on "Waiting for you to submit the form", even though the execution has already completed successfully. Refreshing the editor page clears the waiting state and allows me to test the workflow again. ### To Reproduce 1. Create a new workflow with a Form Trigger connected to an Edit Fields node. 2. Click Execute Workflow. 3. Open the Form Trigger's Test URL. 4. Submit the form. 5. Observe the editor. ### Expected behavior After submitting the form, the editor should receive the execution update, stop waiting and display the completed nodes and their outputs. ### Debug Info # Debug info ## core - n8nVersion: 2.47.5 - platform: docker (self-hosted) - nodeJsVersion: 26.13.0 - nodeEnv: production - database: sqlite - executionMode: regular - concurrency: -1 - license: enterprise (production) - consumerId: 347b2959-28bf-4d1c-987d-717b5a80fcc3 ## storage - success: all - error: all - progress: false - manual: true - binaryMode: filesystem ## pruning - enabled: true - maxAge: 336 hours - maxCount: 10000 executions ## client - userAgent: mozilla/5.0 (windows nt 10.0; win64; x64) applewebkit/537.36 (khtml, like gecko) chrome/156.0.0.0 safari/537.36 edg/156.0.0.0 - isTouchDevice: false ## cluster - instanceCount: 1 - versions: 2.47.5 - instances: - instanceKey: f6632aec-d735-4b32-9de1-0e99b0a81af1, hostId: main-63120ca68f6f, instanceType: main, instanceRole: leader, version: 2.47.5 - checks: - check: hostid-clash, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: lifecycle, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: split-brain, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: version-mismatch, status: succeeded, warnings: - Generated at: 2026-11-13T04:48:55.777Z ### Operating System Windows 11 pro ### n8n Version 2.46.7 and 2.47.5 ### Node.js Version v26.13.0 ### Database SQLite (default) ### Execution mode main (default) ### Hosting self hosted

comments.author: Arin004joshi
comments.text:
Hey @tolani-co. Thanks for reporting the issue. I tested the Form Trigger workflow locally(not the docker setup tho) and on a cloud-hosted n8n instance, but un/fortunately, it worked as expected. Could it be a real time communication issue in your backend? 
Refer this: line 85 in [FormTriggerV2.node.ts](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Form/v2/FormTriggerV2.node.ts)

comments.author: blucca
comments.text:
Building on Arin's native/Cloud check: in **2.47.5**, the editor clears this exact waiting flag in [`testWebhookReceived`](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/n8n%402.47.5/packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/app/composables/usePushConnection/handlers/testWebhookReceived.ts#L16-L19) when the message's `workflowId` matches the current editor document.

Could you repeat the test once with DevTools → Network open on the **editor's `/rest/push` connection**, and report:

- Does a `testWebhookReceived` message arrive? If yes, its `workflowId` and `executionId` fields are enough.
- Is the saved execution #33's `mode` **`manual`** or **`webhook`**?

Those observations give us a specific point to trace between test registration, push delivery and the editor's workflow-ID match. The pinned backend uses `manual` for a test webhook and `webhook` for a production webhook, so the saved mode is a useful second control alongside the message.

comments.author: grinem
comments.text:
Hi @tolani-co,

Building on @blucca's `/rest/push` check, on **Docker + Windows 11** this stuck *"Waiting for you to submit the form"* state almost always comes from one of two origin/WebSocket mismatches between the editor and the container:

1. **Host Origin Mismatch (`localhost` vs `127.0.0.1`):**  
   If your editor tab is open on `localhost:5678` while `WEBHOOK_URL` / the Form Test URL resolves to `127.0.0.1:5678` (or vice versa), the browser session/push channel won't match the incoming `testWebhookReceived` event. Make sure both the canvas URL and `WEBHOOK_URL` use the exact same host.

2. **Explicit Docker Push & Base URL Env Vars:**  
   In your `docker-compose.yml`, explicitly pin the push backend and base URLs:
```yaml
environment:
  - N8N_HOST=localhost
  - N8N_PORT=5678
  - N8N_PROTOCOL=http
  - WEBHOOK_URL=[http]://localhost:5678/
  - N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL=[http]://localhost:5678/
  - N8N_PUSH_BACKEND=websocket
```
*(If you're sitting behind Nginx/Caddy/Traefik on Windows, make sure `Upgrade` and `Connection "upgrade"` headers are forwarded and `proxy_buffering off;` is set so `/rest/push` doesn't stall.)*

If `/rest/push` shows `101 Switching Protocols` in DevTools -> Network -> WS and `testWebhookReceived` still never arrives after pinning `N8N_PUSH_BACKEND=websocket`, sharing the `/rest/push` frame screenshot will pinpoint whether it's an event emission or session-ID issue.
